policy: Actual Sliver implementation, including operator commands, is hostile. Dependencies, fixtures, isolated package declarations and ordinary source are evaluated on their own bytes.

improvements.change: Descriptions identify threat intelligence monitoring and network-query forwarding precisely. Import/type-bound AST coverage accepts assignment, variable declaration, return, expression and if-initializer forms. License callbacks accept variable and return forms. Four original Sliver samples remain hostile.

Calls to NewBotAPI and NewMessage surface as client/message construction helpers. Descriptions for messaging call-name helpers identify the operation without claiming exfiltration or proving network transmission.

Generic keys, identifiers, UUIDs, URL references, configuration copy and lifecycle syntax moved out of malware-family or malicious-intent homes; consumers updated. Structured matching excludes comments and quoted source examples for map lookups, random comparisons and dash arrays.

PR-event workflows with literal title/body interpolation into run scripts produce a suspicious command-injection risk finding. Safe environment indirection and push-only controls do not. This is a source vulnerability observation, not proof of intentional malware or exploitation.

StackRox archive retains one TLS-verification-disable finding. DefraDB archive gains one real PR-input command-interpolation risk finding. Both remain good packages under the triage policy for unusual isolated source risks.
